topStory.headline: Lawyers Hub Launches Africa A.I. Policy Fellowship for Governance Professionals
topStory.summary:
Lawyers Hub has launched the Africa A.I. Policy Fellowship, a three-month program designed to develop emerging and mid-career professionals in artificial intelligence governance and regulatory frameworks, according to Global South Opportunities. The fellowship combines academic training, mentorship, and hands-on policy engagement, targeting policy analysts, legal professionals, researchers, academics, technology specialists, and development practitioners.

The program explicitly focuses on developing policy recommendations tailored to African contexts, recognizing that A.I. governance frameworks developed in other regions may not directly translate. The fellowship emphasizes bridging the gap between academic learning and real-world policy engagement.

The application process is designed to be accessible at seven minutes, and the three-month intensive format targets working professionals who need focused, practical training rather than comprehensive degree programs. The fellowship emphasizes building networks of professionals capable of influencing national and regional policy discussions.

stories.headline: NPR: Faculty and Students Create Divergent A.I. Classroom Policies
stories.summary: An NPR report finds college faculty and students are creating divergent A.I. policies. Professor Dan Cryer at Johnson County Community College opposes A.I. in writing, comparing it to "bringing a forklift to the gym." Professor Leslie Clement at Johnson C. Smith University embraces A.I. as a "powerful collaborator" and co-created a course on "African Diaspora and AI."

stories.headline: College Board: 84% of Faculty Say A.I. Undermines Critical Thinking
stories.summary: College Board research surveying 3,000+ faculty finds 74% report students using A.I. to write essays, with 84% agreeing A.I. reduces critical thinking and originality, according to the College Board. Faculty at selective institutions and writing-intensive disciplines express significantly greater concerns than STEM and business faculty.

stories.headline: UC Irvine Launches A.I. in Higher Education Course for Faculty
stories.summary: The UCI Digital Learning Lab and School of Education will launch an Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education course for instructors starting summer 2026, according to New University. The online course, delivered synchronously over Zoom, is tailored for faculty, lecturers, and supporting staff seeking to integrate A.I. into their teaching.
